item.title: Santa Monica Council Unanimously Approves Sweeping Zoning Overhaul to Boost Business
item.description: Santa Monica City Council unanimously approved zoning changes to streamline business permits, reduce costs from $10K to $8K, and boost economic investment.

item.title: Around Town: Spring Flinging Forward with Padel, Pottery & Persian Flavors
item.description: Spring events in Santa Monica include padel courts grand opening March 5, Persian restaurant at former Izzy's Deli, pottery fundraiser, and Montana Ave shopping.

item.title: Performance Duo Returns After 18 Years for Limited Engagement at 18th Street Arts Center
item.description: Performance artists Rochelle Fabb and Joan Spitler reunite for 'And This' at 18th Street Arts Center in Santa Monica March 8 after 18-year hiatus.

item.title: SMC to Host Talk by Artist Rafa Esparza
item.description: Santa Monica College presents free talk by Mexican-American artist Rafa Esparza on March 11 at 11:10 AM, discussing heritage and identity themes.

item.title: Japanese Arcade Pop-Up 'Gacha & Catch' Reopens on Third Street Promenade
item.description: Japanese arcade pop-up Gacha & Catch reopens March 14 on Santa Monica's Third Street Promenade with exclusive Sonic & Friends collection and UFO claw machines.

item.title: Defense attorneys for Palisades Fire suspect seek release, cite new evidence of LAFD failures
item.description: Defense attorneys for the man accused of sparking the deadly Palisades Fire said Thursday that new evidence — including conflicting firefighter testimony about whether hot spots were fully extinguished before the blaze reignited — undermines the federal case against their client and called for his immediate release from custody.Jonathan
